{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABbmlCew", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhFKKRw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 91, "title": "Implement CD-block compatibility for guest-executed CDC/GFS-style file initialization and reads", "body": "## Problem

The project now has a substantial emulated CD block and a **synthetic external-firmware boot path**. [#83/#84](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/84) proved hardware-driven initial loading; [#85/#86](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/86) extended that firmware to discover the Saturn first-read program via its own SH-2 IP/ISO9660 parsing, without hardcoding the file extent.

**The next obstacle toward software/game compatibility is runtime CD file I/O after the loaded program starts.** Existing synthetic startup proves one bounded boot-file handoff, not that an executing application can initialize the CD library, discover additional files, open/seek/read them repeatedly, and handle independent command completion, CD-buffer routing and errors as software using Sega's CD communication interface (CDC) and file system library (GFS) expects.

**Important interface distinction:** CDC and GFS are software libraries used by Saturn applications, not an automatically available host syscall or a general BIOS-resident file API. The emulator's compatibility responsibility is to reproduce the underlying **guest-visible CD block, registers, responses, buffering, interrupts, DMA and time-dependent behavior**. Author original guest-side library/routines to exercise documented CDC/GFS-style interactions; do **not** intercept library entry points or claim binary compatibility with Sega SDK binaries without independently verifying that contract. Existing HLE system-service entry points are separate and must be preserved.

The task must **implement a concrete hardware compatibility improvement exposed by a pre-change failing guest trace**, not just add a demo or document limitations. This is a bounded increment rather than full Sega CD software library, stock BIOS, authenticated disc or commercial title compatibility.

## Expected outcome

An **original, MIT-licensed guest program** booted using the now-merged synthetic ExternalBios path executes its own **CDC/GFS-style runtime file reader**, using documented CD I/F commands and real emulated hardware to:

1. Initialize/query the drive and its command/response, status and selected ECC/retry parameters, to the extent specified in the primary manual.
2. Enumerate or resolve independently authored ISO9660 runtime data files by name/ID through guest-controlled directory/record reads (reuse the established genuine hardware path; do not have Rust/JS provide file IDs).
3. Open a file handle, seek to another position, read partial and multiple consecutive sectors/byte ranges, close, reopen and read a second file while preserving independent handle/cursor and data-buffer lifetimes.
4. Use actual CD-sector acquisition, filters/selectors/partitions and host FIFO or SCU DMA transfer with documented HIRQ, command-completion/transfer fences and bounded wait behavior; validate actual file bytes and a visible guest effect derived from the loaded data.
5. Recover correctly from a documented abort/reset/media error and repeat after cold boot or SYSRES. Support multiple original disc layouts without special-casing test file names, signatures or contents in production code.

Prefer the **smallest primary-backed, high-impact hardware extension** needed to make these interactions work. Provide a clear supported subset and follow-up limitations rather than overextending into every GFS function or general Sega BIOS execution.

## Context and reproduction

Repository: [takahirox/saturn-rust](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust). Checked `main`: `db96e2d90826e22d6f3568af478ae9b44fd2e27e`. No open Issues or PRs were found when preparing this task.

Start by inspecting actual code, existing tests, and the source Issue's scope:

- [`docs/external-startup.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/external-startup.md), [`docs/validation-issue-85.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/validation-issue-85.md), and original `tests/fixtures/external-startup.s`, `tests/external_startup.rs`, `scripts/external-discovery.mjs`: prior hardware boot discovery; avoid redoing that milestone.
- [`docs/hardware-conformance.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/hardware-conformance.md) **CD, boot and SMPC** inventory: existing command/status/HIRQ, directory acquisition, sector pool, selectors, partitions, FIFO, SCU DMA, TOC and error cases; complete command-specific timing, transfer overlap and software-level CD ABI remain incomplete.
- `src/cd.rs`, `src/media.rs`, `src/disc.rs`, `src/scu.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/wasm.rs`, `tests/cd.rs`, `tests/cd_filesystem.rs`, `tests/cd_directory_schedule.rs`, `tests/external_startup.rs`, `scripts/browser-smoke.mjs`, and `scripts/ci-runner.test.mjs`.
- [`src/hle/README.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/src/hle/README.md): independent guest-executed system/backup services; **no generic CD-library service yet**. Do not install HLE services in ExternalBios mode or copy proprietary routines.
- Relevant primary Sega specifications: [CD Communication I/F ST-162-062094](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-162-062094.pdf), [Saturn Disc Format ST-040-R4](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-040-R4-051795.pdf), [System Program ST-162-R1](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-162-R1-092994.pdf), applicable SCU and CD final revisions. The [Sega CD I/F library architecture](https://manualzz.com/doc/7267353/sega-system-library--smpc-i-f--cd-communication-interface...) distinguishes application GFS/CDC software from hardware CD-block commands. [Sega developer notice STN-19](https://docs.exodusemulator.com/Archives/SSDDV25/segahtml/info/hon/stn19.htm) says GFS initialization performs CDC initialization and changes ECC/retry configuration. Validate exact supported command parameters and manual revisions before coding; examples are **not permission to fabricate software library behavior**.

**Pre-change reproduction requirement:** build an original runtime-file-access guest/ISO where the inherited `main` fails at a **specific documented CD hardware operation or timing/result oracle** while the earlier synthetic firmware successfully discovers and loads the application. Identify the first genuine hardware mismatch; avoid simply deliberately calling an unsupported made-up GFS opcode or marking a fixture incomplete. If the initially chosen happy path already works, broaden the independent CDC/GFS interaction trace to a primary-backed missing case (e.g., initialization parameter lifetime, multiple file/partition ownership, a transfer/interrupt deadline, partial-read resumption or error cancellation) and implement the smallest real underlying fix.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Scope and specification table:** document exact guest-invoked operations, Sega CDC/GFS concepts, their distinction from BIOS/system services, corresponding **real hardware commands and register states**, expected returns/status, time and error boundaries, and primary manual sections. Identify one reproducible inherited-main hardware failure and justify the minimal production fix. Do not claim Sega SDK binary ABI matching or ROM execution where only equivalent original guest semantics are tested.
- [ ] **Working production hardware implementation:** implement a meaningful behavior correction/extension in the actual CD/bus/SCU/device path for the documented failing case, with real state transitions, CD command responses, buffer ownership, DMA/FIFO, HIRQ/SCU acknowledgment and deadlines as relevant. No host intercepts, hardcoded asset contents, software-only fake pass states, constant-success device replies or silent swallowing of unsupported requests.
- [ ] **Guest-executed runtime file API:** create/reuse a small original MIT-licensed SH-2 software library exposing a clear *test-level* init, find/name-to-ID, open, seek, read, close/reopen interface. Exercise actual CD commands while guest-executed; run it **after** the firmware-driven initial executable handoff from #85. Document which pieces are conceptually CDC/GFS-like and which APIs are **not** claimed to be the original Sega ABI.
- [ ] **Meaningful file and layout matrix:** reproduce at least two independent Saturn-IP/ISO9660 disc layouts with multiple non-boot files, changed directory ordering/extent and distinct file lengths; include sector-aligned and non-sector-aligned reads, reads crossing sector boundaries, seeks, repeat reads and alternating files/handles. The same guest/reader binary must find and read the authored data rather than relying on fixture-specific LBA constants. If files larger than current 64 KiB boot bounds are tested, keep the boot-file bound separate from runtime-file support.
- [ ] **Independent byte/output checks:** assert complete actual data bytes (including tails), file cursor/length, unchanged neighboring RAM, guest-calculated checksums/arithmetic and a real Canvas/visible or audio observable influenced by loaded runtime assets. Check actual HIRQ, SCU interrupts, DMA/source/destination transactions and command/sector states with literal expectations independent from production logic. At least one inherited-main negative oracle must fail for the intended reason and pass unchanged after the production implementation.
- [ ] **Timing and error controls:** test slow/pending commands, transfer end, cancel/abort, reset during a transfer, empty/no media, invalid file ID/name, missing/invalid directory record, truncated/corrupted sector, EOF/short read, close/reopen and optional medium replacement. No stale data publication, unbounded polling, duplicate DMA/IRQ acknowledgment or apparent success on errors. Compare scheduling chunks 1/3/17/10000 and passive inspection, and verify proper behavior across supported cold restart and SYSRES.
- [ ] **Cross-mode and privacy preservation:** the genuine ExternalBios path uses the selected original firmware and medium, not HLE-installed service pointers. Existing BIOS-less HLE games and tests keep their original behavior; no regression in Star Collector, Prism Courier, Hardware Lab, backup/controller/audio/Canvas and local-file privacy/asset allowlist. Neither Sega firmware nor proprietary SDK binaries nor retail game content is needed.
- [ ] **Full registered automation:** add original fixture builders/checks and native/production Wasm Chromium smoke coverage, update browser group/shard inventory and CI runner regression counts without dropping old commands or tests. Preserve complete hardware, failure propagation, lossless test transport, artifact identity and main-only GitHub Pages publishing gates. Add focused deterministic native/wait-state tests rather than bloating redundant slow suites; keep the documented test/CI performance principles.
- [ ] **Final implementation validation:** pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native all-target and Wasm `cargo clippy --locked ... -- -D warnings`, `sh scripts/check-fixtures.sh`, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, `node --test scripts/ci-runner.test.mjs`, and full `npm run test:browser`; require all applicable PR GitHub Actions checks before merge. Record actual counts/durations/negative controls and explain any corrected failed attempts. No reduced tests, artificial timeout inflation, blanket retries, required human review, physical console or live Pages verification.
- [ ] **Honest reproducible documentation:** add `docs/validation-issue-91.md` (use actual Issue number), update `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/hardware-conformance.md` and focused CD reference documentation. Record the supported CD command subset, library-style guest behavior, exact hardware fixes, validated layouts, explicit unsupported operations, relevant fixed-width/timing conventions and limits. **Commercial game, genuine Sega BIOS, full CDC/GFS SDK binary, authenticated-disc and complete CD-block compatibility remain unverified.**

## Optional validation

Extended ISO9660/XA or mixed-mode media, buffered CD-DA while streaming, additional nonblocking GFS-like requests, randomized but independently expected file layouts, and safe performance profiling may be useful as long as they are bounded and do not compromise the mandatory current scope. Do not introduce a proprietary Sega SDK dependency, physical-hardware or human test gate.

## Required post-merge verification

None. All mandatory implementation/PR checks must be completed before merge; no deployed-site inspection, actual BIOS/media upload or manual approval is required.

## Related work

Follow-up to [#83/#84](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/84), [#85/#86](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/86), [#75/#76](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/pull/76) and the incomplete Saturn hardware scope originally grouped under #17 (administratively closed as a partial checkpoint, **not** completed hardware conformance). The objective is **runtime CD hardware compatibility for application-level file-library patterns**, not a claim of executing retail software.
